question: What CEU3Minimap draws and does, and how the map mode buttons switch the map, look, and say

addresses.name: CEU3Gui_CreateMinimap
addresses.signature: CEU3Minimap* __stdcall CEU3Gui_CreateMinimap(CGui* gui@ESI, Hoi3CString* name@EDX, void* parent@stack:4) @EAX
addresses.comment: **Makes the minimap element from an `iconType` by name.** Looks the type up through the gui's type tree (+0x34, its slot 1, Find(name)), news 0x120 bytes and runs CEU3Minimap::CEU3Minimap(new, gui +0x30 (the graphics), gui, parent) with the type in EDX, then appends the object to the gui's element vector (+0x5C, 0x8DDBE0). `ret 4`. Two callers, both for `minimap_pic`: CInGameIdler::Enter (VA 0x65F99A, kept at CInGameIdler +0x1920) and CInGameIdler::ReloadMenubar (VA 0x6595EB, the same slot). The only way a CEU3Minimap is made, which is why exactly one exists. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x6435E0 to the `ret 4` at 0x643663. Callers by findRefs --callers: exactly 0x6595EB and 0x65F99A, each preceded by the string 'minimap_pic' and followed by a store to +0x186C (on idler+0xB4) / +0x1920. Wrong if a third caller turns up or the type lookup is not gui+0x34 slot 1.

addresses.name: CEU3Minimap::CEU3Minimap
addresses.signature: CEU3Minimap* __stdcall CEU3Minimap::CEU3Minimap(CEU3Minimap* this@stack:4, CEU3Graphics* graphics@stack:8, CGui* gui@stack:0xC, void* parent@stack:0x10, void* type@EDX) @EAX
addresses.comment: Calls CIcon::CIcon (rva 0x6A1C00) at 0x67A47D, then `mov [esi], 0x15cf15c`. The one live instance is the iconType named minimap_pic, which is why a CEU3Minimap turns up in CGui+0x5C alongside twelve RTTI-less widget classes.  **The arguments, read 2026-11-07**: this, the graphics (the gui's +0x30 - screen size at +0x6B9BC/+0x6B9C0), the gui, the parent, and the iconType in EDX; `ret 0x10`. After CIcon::CIcon it keeps: +0xF0 the graphics global [VA 0x1A85634], +0xF4 the gui, +0xF8 the parent, +0xFC the map graphics owner [VA 0x1A855FC], **+0x100 the map camera** (the owner's +4, which the CInGameIdler constructor points at its own +0x1938), then makes **two line objects** through Graphics_CreateLineObject on +0xF0 - +0x118 the camera frame and +0x11C one never given a point - each with width 1.0 (its +0x1134 and ID3DXLine::SetWidth) and shown (slot 13); and +0x110/+0x114 = float(CMap +0x2A74/+0x2A78), the map's width and height (5616, 2160). Its only maker is CEU3Gui_CreateMinimap. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x67A3C0..0x67A595. The four stack arguments line up with CEU3Gui_CreateMinimap's pushes (eax=new, edx=[gui+0x30], esi=gui, ecx=its own stack argument) and the type with its EDX; the stores to +0xF0..+0x11C are in the listing. Revised: adds the signature and the fields; nothing earlier is contradicted.

addresses.comment: Puts CEU3Minimap's two vftables back, hands both line objects (+0x118, +0x11C) to the graphics' remover (0xA6FCA0, with the graphics +0xF0 in ESI), then CIcon's destructor (0xAA21A0). `this` on the stack, `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CEU3Minimap::Update
addresses.comment: **CEU3Minimap slot 6, run on every shown element each frame by CGui::ProcessInput: redraws the camera frame when the camera or the minimap has moved.** The mouse argument is not read. Nothing happens unless the map camera's x_settled (+0x33C), y_settled (+0x340) or height (+0x348) differ from the copies at +0x104/+0x108/+0x10C, or the minimap's position (slot 70) differs from a function-local static pair (VA 0x1BEB590/594, set on the first call). Then it keeps the three and the position, empties both line objects (+0x1114 = 0) and gives +0x118 five points, a closed rectangle: fx = x_settled / map width (+0x110), fy = y_settled / map height (+0x114); (w, h) = the minimap's size (slot 61, shorts); centre cx = pos.x + fx*w - [VA 0x1BEA498] (a .bss float nothing writes, so 0), cy = pos.y + (h - fy*h - 4) - **y flipped, the map's y running north**; t = height / (highest - lowest) (+0x348 / (+0x350 - +0x34C)), half width hw = int(t*1410 + 70) * 0.1 * 0.25, half height hh = int(t*820 + 80) * 0.1 * 0.25; corners truncated to int: (cx-hw, cy-hh), (cx-hw, cy+hh), (cx+hw, cy+hh), (cx+hw, cy-hh), (cx-hw, cy-hh). So **the frame's size is a straight line in the camera's height, not a projection of the view**, and nothing clips it or wraps it at the minimap's edges. +0x11C is never given a point. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read whole 0x67A650..0x67AB64. Constants read off the image: 1410.0, 70.0, 820.0, 80.0 (doubles at VA 0x160A338/330/328/320), 0.1 as a float widened (0x160A3C0), 0.25 (0x160A258), -4.0 (0x160A428). 0x1BEA498 has one reference in .text (this read) and lies in .data's uninitialised tail. Slot 6 = Update per CGui::ProcessInput's record. Wrong if the two comparisons against +0x33C/+0x340 are against the look pair +0x334/+0x338 instead - they are not, in the listing.

addresses.name: CEU3Minimap::Show

So the frame comes and goes with the minimap. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 1.

addresses.name: CEU3Minimap::HandleMouse
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CEU3Minimap::HandleMouse(CEU3Minimap* this, void* event, int unused)
addresses.comment: **CEU3Minimap slot 1, the minimap's whole answer to the mouse, replacing GuiButton_HandleMouse and never calling it.** Only a mouse event (+8 == 0) on a shown minimap (+0x2C) that is a **left press** (+0x10 == 3, +0x14 == 1) does anything; moves, releases, the right and middle buttons fall through unhandled. The pointer (the event's +0xC object, slot 19, two ints) less the minimap's position truncated (slot 70) gives (rx, ry), taken only where **0 < rx < w and 0 < ry < h**, strictly, (w, h) the minimap's size (slot 61). Then x = (rx - 1.0) * (map width / w) and y = (h - (ry - 1.0)) * (map height / h), the width and height the map graphics owner's +0x60D4/+0x60D8 (copies of CMap +0x2A74/+0x2A78, 5616 and 2160), and MapCamera_JumpTo(&(x, y), camera +0x100) - **the camera is put there at once, its height untouched**; the event is marked handled (+0x18 = 1), which takes it off the frame's list so the map never sees the press. No sound, no drag, no tooltip of its own. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Read whole 0x67AC00..0x67AE00. Slot 1 of CEU3Minimap's table is this, where CIcon's slot 1 is GuiButton_HandleMouse (0xACFBE0) - read off both tables. The 1.0 is the double at VA 0x160A248. Wrong if a move event (+0x10 other than 3) reaches the JumpTo: the four gates at 0x67AC15..0x67AC33 all jump to the epilogue.

addresses.name: MapCamera_JumpTo
addresses.comment: **Puts the map camera on a point at once**: unless the camera's frozen byte (+0x356) is set, x and y (+0x334/+0x338) and x_settled and y_settled (+0x33C/+0x340) all take the point's two floats, so the move is not eased. The height is not touched. Bare `ret`. One direct caller, CEU3Minimap::HandleMouse (VA 0x67ADEE). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Read whole 0x63D3C0..0x63D3F2; findRefs --callers gives exactly one call, at 0x67ADEE. Every operand is in the listing.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::HourlyUpdate
addresses.comment: **Slot 52, the in-game screen's hourly hook**: called every hour, unconditionally, at the end of RunHourlyTick (VA 0x68240D, `[state +0xBE8]` slot 52). Its whole work: where the day/night overlay `minimap_overlay` (+0x191C) exists, its frame (slot 18) = (CCurrentGameState +0xBDC - 43,800,000) mod 24 - **the hour of the day**. Returns true, bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Read whole 0x661BC0..0x661C92; vtable.py --holding: CInGameIdler slot 52 only. The call at 0x68240D..0x68241B is in RunHourlyTick's last block (cfg: reached from 0x6823E5/0x6823F7 with no condition on the hour). 0x29C55C0 = 43,800,000 = 1,825,000 x 24.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_CloseCountryView
addresses.comment: Closes country view `index` (+0xD00[index], its slots 5 and 4), hides `bg_main_menus` (+0x1914) and **shows the minimap, `minimap_bg` and `minimap_overlay` again** (+0x1920, +0x1918, +0x191C, slot 13, the last as a tail jump). The counterpart of CInGameIdler::OpenCountryView, which hides those three. Callers at VA 0x41EA6E, 0x678243 and 0x7D9948. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Read whole 0x665220..0x665272 (ends `jmp eax`). The behaviour is in the listing; the name - which of the three callers closes which view - rests on OpenCountryView's record, so inferred. Wrong if a caller passes something other than a view index in EDI.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::ReloadMenubar
addresses.comment: **Slot 0 of the CReloadDispatcher table CInGameIdler carries at +0xB4: makes the menubar's pieces again from the gui.** `this` is the idler + 0xB4, so every offset in it is 0xB4 short of the idler's. Among the rest (`menubar`, `chat_list`, the message log and chat windows): the old `bg_main_menus`, `minimap_bg`, `minimap_pic` and `minimap_overlay` are deleted (slot 12) and made again - `bg_main_menus` and hidden (idler +0x1914), `minimap_bg` (+0x1918, gui slot 31, shown), **`minimap_pic` through CEU3Gui_CreateMinimap** (+0x1920, shown), `minimap_overlay` (+0x191C, gui slot 31) - then the overlay's frame set to the hour of the day as CInGameIdler::HourlyUpdate does, and shown. Returns true, bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: 0x658EC0 abuts CInGameIdler_Render's `ret 4` at 0x658EBD (no padding - trap 2); vtable.py --holding: CInGameIdler slot 0 at object offset 180 (0xB4), whose base there is CReloadDispatcher. gui = [ebx-0x54] = idler +0x60, which is what slot 14 answers. Read from 0x6594B8 to the `ret` at 0x65975D; the menubar half before it only skimmed for its names.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::DoTutorialAction
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CInGameIdler::DoTutorialAction(CInGameIdler* this, Hoi3CString* key, Hoi3CString* value, void* unknown, int number)
addresses.comment: **Slot 81: a named action on the in-game screen, as a tutorial page gives it.** `ret 0x10`. Compares the key with `close_all`, `diplomacy`, `industry`, `div_designer`, `div_designer_armor`, `technology`, `politics`, `intel`, `ledger`, `message_log`, `units`, `province` / `open`, `zoom`, `mapmode`, `exclusive` / `yes` and others; **`mapmode` calls a map mode's button setter by the value**: `terrain` MapMode_Terrain_Set, `political` the political setter, `diplomacy` the diplomatic, `region` MapMode_Region_Set, **`culture` MapMode_Supply_Colour (the supply setter - an EU3 name left on it)**, `theatre` the theatre setter, `strength` the strength setter; any other value does nothing. `zoom` hands float(number) to 0x63D350 on the map camera (not read). Only the `mapmode` arm was read through. Its one known caller is VA 0x8E560D in the unrecorded 0x8E4490, which passes 'mapmode' and the page's +0x1A8 string - and `tutorial/chapter1.txt` pages carry `mapmode = "terrain"` and `zoom = 200`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: 0x64B2D0 opens `push ebp` on the byte after slot 80's `ret 4` at 0x64B2CD, with no padding (trap 2); retsBefore from 0x64ACB0 shows `ret 4` up to 0x64B2CD and `ret 0x10` from 0x64B3FD, which cannot be one function. vtable.py --holding: CInGameIdler slot 81. The 'mapmode' arm 0x64B925..0x64BA66 read whole. The tutorial reading of the caller is inferred from the string arguments.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::SetAirOrdersMapMode
addresses.comment: **Slot 100: map mode 15, the air orders window's.** The air and naval icons down when leaving 18 or 19 (as every setter), the idler's +0xD34 and CMap +0x2A90 = 15, the settings' +0xE7 = 0, layer mask +0xF0 = 0xFFBA and map style +0xF4 = 16. **No sound, no MapMode_ShowButton and no colouring** - the window colours the map itself (0x867DB0) - so the button that was down stays down. Called by CAirOrdersView::CAirOrdersView right after PushMapMode (VA 0x741132, 0x74119C); the window's destructor pops the mode (VA 0x741688). Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Read whole 0x677380..0x677401; vtable.py --holding: CInGameIdler slot 100. The 0xF loaded at 0x6773C1. The two vcalls in CAirOrdersView::CAirOrdersView are [edx+0x188] and [edx+0x190] on the game state's +0xBE8.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::SetTheatreEditing
addresses.comment: **Slot 110: map mode 17, the theatre editor, on and off.** Given a headquarters: +0x7C = it, PushMapMode, the air and naval icons down as every setter, +0xD34 and CMap +0x2A90 = 17, settings +0xE7 = 0, layer mask 0xFFBE, map style 2, the graphics owner's +0x60F8 = 0, HideProvinceObjects98, the theatre colouring (VA 0x865290), Map_RefreshColourTextures(0), +0x60DC = 1. **No MapMode_ShowButton.** Given null: PopMapMode, then where +0x7C was set and the province list (+0x74) is not empty, the edited provinces go out as a command for the headquarters' theatre (CUnit_FindTheatre, `new 0x54`, 0x5EA010) and the list is freed. CInGameIdler_HandleInput's Alt / Ctrl+R with a theatre headquarters selected alone calls it. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 5.

addresses.name: MapMode_Terrain_Set
addresses.comment: **The terrain map mode's setter** (mode 0, button `mapmode_1`, bound through the glue at CInGameIdler +0xD38). Unless the mode is already 0, the `click` sound where it is not already playing (the sound's slot 25, then slot 9); the air icons and circles down when leaving 18 (HideAirMapIcons, ClearAirBaseCircles), the naval icons down (0x46AA70) when leaving 19; the idler's +0xD34 and CMap +0x2A90 = 0; **MapMode_ShowButton(1)**; the settings' layer mask +0xF0 = 0xFFFF, map style +0xF4 = 0 and +0xE7 = 0; HideProvinceObjects98; the graphics owner's +0x60F9 = 0; MapMode_Terrain_Colour; Map_RefreshColourTextures(0); the graphics owner's +0x60DC = 1. Bare `ret`. Also what PopMapMode runs for a popped 0, 14, 15 or 16, what DoTutorialAction's `mapmode terrain` runs, and what CInGameIdler_RefreshMap runs in mode 0 when the refresh flags have any of 0xF but are not exactly 2 - which is how a new session's first frame paints the terrain mode. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 5.

addresses.name: MapMode_ShowButton
addresses.comment: Shows which map mode button is down: every one of `mapmode_1` to `mapmode_16` to frame 1, then `mapmode_` and the number given to frame 2. First, where the settings' +0xF0 & +0xEC has 0x1, every 0x24-byte entry of the graphics owner's +0x1EF8 (counted at +0x1EF4) gets -1 and 0x862260 runs. The air mode gives 15. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airmap.md, section 1. **The number is the button's own** (1..16, not the game's mode): every button setter passes its button - terrain 1, political 2, weather 3, intel 4, revolt 5, diplomatic 6, region 7, supply 8, infrastructure 9, VP 10, theatre 11, strength 12, resources 13, simplified terrain 14, air 15, naval 16 - and CInGameIdler::Enter calls it with 1 just after binding the buttons (VA 0x65E588). The frames are the button's slot 18 (SetFrame): 1 up, 2 down, the two halves of each `mapmode_*` sprite (noOfFrames = 2). The modes with no button - 14 (placing a deployment), 15 (air orders), 17 (theatre editor) - never call it, so the last button pressed stays down under them. Nothing hides or greys a map mode button: `mapmode_1`..`mapmode_16` are named only here, in Enter's binding and in GetElementTooltip. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: The 16 push values read off each setter's call (setters.py summary over all 16 bound setters). String references: each of 'mapmode_1'..'mapmode_16' has exactly three in .text (0x65D..., 0x665..., 0x6C8...), plus 'mapmode_8' a fourth at 0x6568C8 (CInGameIdler::Update, not followed). So a screen is born in mode 0. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 7.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::PushMapMode

Three users in the image, each paired with a PopMapMode: placing a deployment (SetDeploymentBeingPlaced, mode 14), the air orders window (CAirOrdersView::CAirOrdersView then SetAirOrdersMapMode, mode 15; the destructor pops) and the theatre editor (SetTheatreEditing, mode 17). The list is a stack - the newest mode first. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Every access to +0xAB8/+0xAC0 in a resumed sweep of .text on a CInGameIdler is in the constructor (0x647BED/0x647BF9), PushMapMode and PopMapMode; the slot 98 vcalls ([reg+0x188] on the idler) found at 0x6667D8, 0x741132 and 0x667DEA. Revised: adds the users.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::PopMapMode
addresses.comment: Slot 99: where the list at +0xAB8 is not empty, takes its first mode off and tail-jumps to that mode's setter through a 20-entry table at 0x67545C - 1 political, 2 diplomatic, 18 MapMode_Air_Set, 19 0x6680E0 and the rest; 0, 14, 15 and 16 all go to 0x666020. So a mode 14 popped sets the map to what 0 sets. Bare `ret` where the list is empty. The name is ours. The whole table (VA 0x67545C): 0 MapMode_Terrain_Set, 1 political, 2 diplomatic, 3 MapMode_Region_Set, 4 supply, 5 infrastructure, 6 intel, 7 VP, 8 theatre, 9 strength, 10 MapMode_Resources_Set, 11 weather, 12 revolt, 13 simplified terrain, 14/15/16 terrain, **17 the theatre setter (mode 8)**, 18 air, 19 MapMode_Naval_Set; above 19 terrain. Each is a button's full setter, so the button is pressed again and the `click` plays where the mode changes. Callers: SetDeploymentBeingPlaced(null), SetTheatreEditing(null) and the air orders window's destructor. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-minimap.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: The 20 table entries read off the image and each tail jump followed (0x6753B6..0x675451). Revised: names the entries the old comment left as 'the rest' and adds 17 and 13.

struct_fields.name: mapmode_byte_e7
struct_fields.comment: Written by every map mode setter and the CInGameIdler constructor: 1 by the resources mode alone, 0 by all the others. No reader found next to a GetGameSettings call; what it governs is not established.
struct_fields.evidence: The scan for `call GetGameSettings` followed within six instructions by an access to [eax+0xE7] finds 20 sites, every one a write (the constructor, 18 setters, SetDeploymentBeingPlaced); readers through a held settings pointer would not show in that scan.
